scope: Combined cross-peer and four-profile volatile duplicate/cache-budget acceptance over TCP/TLS; pure Go, no persistence; tests/docs only.

priority_selection.reason: Batch98 prioritized combined cross-peer and mixed-profile duplicate/cache verification. Existing runtime behavior can be exercised without changing cache identity or adding durable storage.

assertions: Origin-Host/E2E identity joins across peers with case-normalized origin; HBH/T/Proxy changes do not create new work.
All six combined constructions preserve normal2001/5012 and E3004 results, per-arrival proxy envelopes and single-charge/single-delivery behavior.
Disconnected primary reports a failed primary write while an admitted duplicate peer receives the committed result.
Content and policy conflicts preserve canonical bytes, record identity, execution/retention deadlines and result authority. Source policy and MaxArrivals apply before a duplicate may join.
Different profiles sharing an Origin/E2E key conflict during processing and after commitment; a different authorized origin creates independent work.
Four logical requests/eight arrivals coexist across combined/S6c/Sh/SGd. Three profiles complete and replay while each fourth profile is delayed, under shared and independent cache classes.
Slot limits leave byte headroom; byte limits use exact compiled reservation sums with spare slots. Cache hits work at capacity; misses cannot evict promised records.
An exhausted independent class does not prevent the other three classes admitting work; shared full cache retains all four profile results.
Explicit timer expiry releases cache charges and permits a new logical record for the old identity. Close/Wait releases all charged resources; monotonic conflict counters remain telemetry.
